title: Emrys and the Bell
premise: Folklorist Vesper Okafor returns to Hollowmere to record its harvest songs, only to find the villagers refuse to sing any of them twice — because a second singing is an invitation. Waiting on her porch is Emrys, the imaginary friend she abandoned at age nine, unchanged after twenty years and hungry for the life she promised him. As the harvest moon rises, Vesper uncovers the truth: as a child she spoke a bargain aloud, and Emrys is the thing the village has been feeding with its unsung songs to keep it from collecting. To survive until sunrise, she must choose between exposing the village's complicity in an old disappearance and paying the debt herself, ending with Vesper singing the song a second time — not to banish Emrys, but to finally name him, freeing both of them at the cost of her belonging in Hollowmere forever.
about_author: Coral Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist of oral histories who spent years transcribing songs people asked never to be printed. She writes horror from a farmhouse where she keeps the doors counted, out of habit rather than fear.

chapters.title: The Song Nobody Sings Twice
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Arriving in Hollowmere, she records a harvest song from an old woman who stops mid-verse, terrified, and begs her to erase the tape. The village's warmth curdles into watchfulness. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional excitement.

chapters.title: Doors Counted, Lights On
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Settling into her rented cottage, her childhood rituals of counting doors and keeping lights burning resurface. A neighbor, Marta, warns her gently not to record after dark. Emotional beat: the comfort and futility of old defenses.

chapters.title: Waiting on the Porch
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At dusk she finds Emrys on the porch — exactly as she left him at nine years old, down to the crooked smile. He greets her like no time has passed. She flees inside and counts the doors twice. Emotional beat: dread wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: What Imaginary Friends Remember
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Emrys speaks through the door all night, recalling promises only she could know. By dawn he is gone, but his voice lingers in the tape recorder's hiss. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into fear.

chapters.title: The Archive of Unsung Things
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In the parish records she finds a pattern: every disappearance in Hollowmere's history falls on a harvest moon, and every witness account mentions 'a boy on the porch.' Emotional beat: scholarly thrill turning cold.

chapters.title: Marta's Debt
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta confesses her family has sung the binding songs for generations — once each, never twice — to keep something fed and contained. She begs Vesper to leave before the moon. Emotional beat: weary, inherited terror.

chapters.title: The Year Vesper Stopped Talking
chapters.summary: Flashback, Vesper's POV. Age nine: a lonely, invisible child invents Emrys, then speaks a bargain aloud at the old well — 'stay with me forever.' Her parents' intervention and the village's silence follow. Emotional beat: aching loneliness.

chapters.title: He Doesn't Age, He Waits
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Emrys appears in daylight now, visible only to her, gently cataloguing everything she's failed to become. He isn't threatening — he's patient, and that is worse. Emotional beat: the horror of being known.

chapters.title: The Well at Wray's Field
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She finds the sealed well and the carved names around its rim — including her own, scratched by a child's hand. The stone is warm. Emotional beat: physical evidence collapsing her skepticism.

chapters.title: Songs as Fences
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Decoding the harvest songs, she realizes they aren't celebrations but a ledger: each verse names what was invited in, and the refusal to sing twice keeps the invitation incomplete. Emotional beat: revelation with terrible implications.

chapters.title: The Missing Okafor Girl
chapters.summary: Village elder Tam's POV. Tam recalls the night young Vesper 'went missing' for three days as a child, and the bargain the village made with her parents to bury the event. Emotional beat: complicity and shame.

chapters.title: He Knows the Words
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Emrys sings the harvest song perfectly — a second time. The village's dogs go silent, lights fail house by house, and Marta pounds on Vesper's door: 'What did you let him do?' Emotional beat: catastrophe triggered.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Rises
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. With the moon up, the village seals its doors, and Emrys tells Vesper the truth plainly: he was invited — by her — and everything since has been the village dodging her debt. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Village Fed
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta reveals the deepest secret: the songs weren't keeping Emrys out — they were keeping him in, and every unsung second verse has been starving him toward the door. Emotional beat: pity entangled with terror.

chapters.title: Sunrise Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She calculates the hours until dawn and what Emrys will do when the moon sets unpaid. He offers her a way out: name another. She refuses. Emotional beat: moral clarity hardening under pressure.

chapters.title: The Second Verse
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Searching the archive, she finds the true second verse — the one the villagers cut out — which doesn't bind Emrys but releases whoever speaks his true name. The name was never his. Emotional beat: hope with a knife's edge.

chapters.title: Doors Opening
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The village's counted doors begin opening one by one despite locks and nails, as Emrys walks the streets collecting on twenty years of withheld song. Emotional beat: siege-like dread.

chapters.title: The Well, Opened
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At the well, Emrys shows her what he was before she named him: a hungry thing the village once fed children to, until a lonely girl's bargain accidentally gave it a shape and a name — and a conscience. Emotional beat: horrifying sympathy.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She confronts the village elders with the truth of their feeding and their treatment of her family. They offer her silence and a place among them if she lets Emrys take Marta's grandson instead. Emotional beat: righteous fury.

chapters.title: Sung Twice
chapters.summary: Climax, Vesper's POV. On the porch where he waited, Vesper sings the harvest song a second time, complete with the true second verse, and speaks Emrys's original name into the moonlight. The thing beneath the name must answer or dissolve. Emotional beat: sacrificial courage.

chapters.title: What the Name Let Go
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The name releases Emrys from her — and her from him. The hungry thing beneath, unshaped and unnamed, cannot cross a threshold no one has invited it over. Dawn comes. The village is spared and will never forgive her. Emotional beat: exhausted, costly relief.

chapters.title: The Folklorist's Last Recording
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Vesper's POV. She leaves Hollowmere with one tape: the full song, sung twice, hers and hers alone. On the highway out, she catches herself humming it — and for the first time, nothing answers. Emotional beat: bittersweet freedom and belonging found in leaving.
